headline: No sector-rotation strategy in this family beats SPY after California tax with good confidence: nothing passes the PROTOCOL section 3 bar in CA or FED, and every CA "edge" is shared by random picks under the same tax-managed execution. The pre-2000 holdout of the incumbent's exact rule on a pre-registered pre-ETF copy of its menu (PRE20) is weakly supportive. On the long protocol it beat VFINX by +0.59 pp (5-year windows) and +0.52 pp (10-year windows). It beat equal-weight and random tax-managed controls in every yearly-start pre-2000 window. Its excess over VFINX falls to between -1.1 and +2.6 pp once fund distributions are taxed yearly, and it wins by the same freeze-into-early-winners mechanism the incumbent uses after 2010. The rule does not transfer across sector universes: on the full protocol in CA it scores -0.72 to +0.15 pp on the five sector-ETF menus (SPDR 9/11, iShares, Vanguard, industry ETFs) and beats on average only 2.5 of 5 site-RandomPicker TaxManagedCombo controls on 8 other menus, though it beats 10 of 10 on its own 22-ETF menu. Pre-tax, fine-grained Fidelity Select industry momentum was strong before 2000 (+5 to +9 pp/yr), roughly halved afterwards, is fragile to costs and parameters, and is absent on coarse sector ETFs. That makes it irrelevant for a taxable account.
findings: CA, standard execution: sector momentum loses after tax. On the Fidelity/Vanguard 32-fund menu (FSEL32, long_screen 1986-2023 vs VFINX) the median CA score is -0.80 pp (132 configs) and -2.7 pp before 2000. Mean reversion (-4.9), seasonality (-4.5), low-vol (-1.8), low-beta (-1.5; pre-2000 5-year windows -7.9), 52-week high (-2.0) and random monthly picks (-3.4) are all worse.

CA, tax-managed execution lifts every rule, not just momentum: tax-managed momentum median +1.28 pp (144 configs), tax-managed random picks +1.11 pp (35), equal-weight tax-managed menu +1.47 pp. With identical execution, momentum's percentile within the random-seed distribution is 0.52-0.80 on score. It is 0.80-0.88 on pre-2000 5-year windows, but only 0.40 on pre-2000 10-year windows and 0.10-0.28 after 2000, where momentum trails random picks by about 1 pp/yr.

On the full protocol (2000-2026 vs SPY, CA), every Fidelity-menu finalist (score +0.83 to +1.89 pp) sits inside the range of 5 random tax-managed pickers on the same menu (+0.37 to +1.82 pp, boot_p 0.045-0.64). The no-selection equal-weight tax-managed control has the best bootstrap: full +1.91 pp, boot_p 0.069. All finalists fail ex10_beat >= 0.75 and ex15_beat >= 0.85.

Incumbent's idea before 2000 (new, pre-registered PRE20 menu: each of the incumbent's 22 ETFs mapped by category to a fund that existed by 1986-96). The exact site rule (12-1, top 5, Q, TaxManagedCombo 1%) in CA scores: long protocol ho5 +0.59 pp (65% of 37 windows above VFINX), ho10 +0.52 pp (59% of 17); long_screen ho5 +1.09 (8/10), ho10 +1.23 (5/5). It beat the median of 10 random tax-managed pickers and the equal-weight tax-managed menu in all 10 five-year and 5 ten-year yearly-start holdout windows. The equal-weight control was negative (long ho10 -1.07 pp, 0% of windows). The 1986-99 monthly path from the 1986 start was flat (+0.03 pp, p 0.51).

Mechanism of the pre-2000 PRE20 result: from a 1986 start the rule froze by about 1990 into health care (FSPHX, 23-32% of the portfolio for 40 years), staples (FDFAX), Dodge & Cox and international, and traded only 2-10 times a year after that. That is the same 'never sell a winner above cost' regime bet the incumbent makes on XLK/QQQ/IWF after 2010. On the sector-only analog FSEL11 the pre-2000 edge is modest (long ho5 +0.42, ho10 +0.72 pp; 60th-90th percentile of random pickers). On the fine-grained FSEL32 it is about the same as the equal-weight control.

Universe robustness on the incumbent's own protocol (full, CA, exact site class) versus the site RandomPicker with the same TaxManagedCombo. Score and beats-out-of-5 random seeds: SPDR9 -0.06 (2/5), SPDR11 -0.10 (3/5), ISH10 -0.72 (2/5), VAN10 -0.56 (5/5), IND16 +0.15 (2/5), FSEL32 +1.13 (4/5), PRE20 +0.14 (2/5), FSEL11 +0.07 (0/5); average 2.5 of 5. On its own INC22 menu the incumbent (+0.66) beats 10 of 10 random pickers (median -0.23, max +0.06), so 12-1 selection mattered there in 2000-2026, but the effect does not transfer to other sector universes.

Realism: Fidelity Select funds distribute about 4-5%/yr (mostly capital gains, often short-term) against about 1.5% for SPY. The engine compounds distributions untaxed until sale. Taxing them yearly (lab realism replay) removes 0.2-0.6 pp/yr (all taxed as qualified, the lab's rule) or 0.5-1.2 pp/yr (half taxed as ordinary) from every Fidelity-menu result after 2000, and 0-1.4 / 0.4-2.7 pp in pre-2000 windows. After this, the incumbent's rule on PRE20 is +0.34/-0.11 pp for 2000-2026 and -0.37/-1.14 pp for 1986-2000. The best CA config (C1) is +0.32/-0.21 pp for 2000-2026.

Pre-tax (NONE, diagnostic): Fidelity industry momentum was strong before 2000. Blend 63/126/252 top 3 M scored ho5 +7.0 pp on long_screen. Across signal lags of 0-10 trading days the six main rules keep scores of +3.6 to +7.4 pp and ho5 of +3.5 to +11.6 pp, so it is not a stale-NAV artifact. Leave-one-out (17 of 32 funds) keeps it at +4.4 to +6.4 pp, and FSEL28 (no Vanguard funds) is about the same.

Pre-tax decay after 2000: the median momentum config's post-2000 monthly excess (+2.0 pp) is about the equal-weight menu's (+2.2 pp). Spearman of pre- vs post-2000 5-year excess across 473 configs is only 0.22. On ETF menus after 2000 (screen, NONE), momentum helps only on fine industry menus (FSEL32 +0.4 to +4.0 pp, IND16 up to +2.4 pp) and not on coarse sector ETFs (SPDR9 -1.5 to +1.0, ISH10 -2.6 to 0.0, VAN10 -2.3 to +0.1). On 20 random 10-ETF menus from BROAD_EQUITY_POOL_2003, momentum minus equal weight is -0.02 pp (45% positive).

Pre-tax finalists are fragile. N1 (FSEL32 blend3 top 3 M) meets criteria 1-3 in NONE on full (score +2.42, ex10_beat 0.93, ex15_beat 1.00, boot_p 0.049), but only 1 of its 4 immediate neighbours does. It also collapses at 30 bp/side commission (long score +2.75, boot_p 0.19) and turns negative at 75 bp, which matters given Select funds' historical loads and fees. N3 (L189 top 5 Q) is cost-robust (+2.71 pp at 75 bp) but misses ex10_beat (0.746), and only 1 of its 3 neighbours passes.

Overfitting diagnostics. On the CA long_screen grid (909 configs) the best config by monthly mean is a random tax-managed control (seed 14). Walk-forward is +3.4 pp on 10/5 (6 decisions, one of them +14.5 pp) but -4.3 pp on 5/3 (oos_beat 0.25). PBO is 0.42 and the best config's deflated Sharpe is 0.043. The NONE long_screen grid gives walk-forward +5.9 pp (10/5) / -0.3 pp (5/3), PBO 0.35, DSR 0.068.

PROTOCOL 5.3 and menu-level controls.
(1) 20 random 10-ETF menus drawn from common.BROAD_EQUITY_POOL_2003 (screen, SPY). Pre-tax blend momentum minus the equal-weight menu: -0.02 pp mean, 45% positive. So the pre-tax momentum effect does not show up on menus nobody chose. (2) Remove-the-star: leave-one-out on FSEL32 (17 of 32 funds done before the cutoff) keeps the NONE score at +4.4 to +6.4 pp; dropping FSPTX (technology) hurts most. In CA, standard-execution leave-one-out ranges -0.3 to +1.1 pp. FSEL28 (without the 4 Vanguard funds) is about the same.

(4) The pre-ETF menus PRE20 and FSEL11 were pre-registered category-for-category in s6_pre.py before any run, to avoid picking pre-2000 winners.
(5) Hindsight-sensitive inputs remain. The Fidelity Select menu contains only funds that survive today (merged or closed Selects are missing), which inflates absolute FSEL results including the equal-weight control (about +2 pp/yr pre-tax vs VFINX). lab_bugs: research/lab/realism.py: record(cfg, regime, start, end) accepts `end`, but RecordingGate keeps recording (and the engine keeps trading) to the data end. _adjust_path then takes the liquidation value at `end` but the wealth path and the years to the data end, so engine_cagr/real_cagr are wrong for any end before 2026-07-01 (mixed horizons). verify.battery always uses the default end, so its numbers are unaffected. Workaround in scratch (a_real.py: a ClippedRecordingGate that stops after `end`); it reproduces cached window excess exactly (e.g. +1.714 pp vs +1.714 pp).
research/lab/realism.py: adjusted() hard-codes SPY as the benchmark (no VFINX option), so the stricter tax check cannot be applied to pre-1993 or long-protocol windows without a wrapper.

research/lab/realism.py: character() classifies every non-bond, non-REIT fund distribution as qualified dividends. For actively managed mutual funds (Fidelity Select etc.) much of each distribution is short-term capital gains taxed at ordinary rates, so the adjustment is lenient; any family using mutual-fund proxies in CA/FED is flattered by about 0.5-1.5 pp/yr even after realism.

research/lab/metrics.py walk_forward(step_quarters=4) steps over protocol start indices. On yearly-start protocols (screen, long_screen) it re-selects every 4 years: 3 out-of-sample decisions for 10/5 on screen, 6 on long_screen, versus 12 on full. Diagnostics on screened grids are therefore coarse.

# Sector rotation with a pre-ETF holdout (`sector_deep`)

Family module: `research/lab/families/sector_deep.py`. It has one signal, `sector_deep.rotate`, and was not edited after stage 1, so all cached results stay valid. Scripts, logs and intermediate tables are in `research/lab/scratch/sector_deep/`. The full results table is `research/lab/results/sector_deep_table.csv`: one row per config x regime x protocol, with a `cfg_json` column holding the exact runnable config.

All excess numbers are after-tax CAGR minus the benchmark's, in percentage points per year (pp), straight from the lab engine (the website's numbers). The benchmark is SPY on `screen`/`full` and VFINX on `long_screen`/`long`. Regimes: CA = 48.1% short-term / 28.1% long-term (primary); FED = 35/15; NONE = no tax (a diagnostic only for this user).

## Verdict

**No sector-rotation strategy in this family beats SPY after California tax with good confidence. Nothing passes the PROTOCOL section 3 bar in CA or FED.**

The key out-of-sample test of the incumbent's idea is 12-1 momentum, top 5, quarterly, with the TaxManagedCombo 1%/yr gain budget. It came out weakly positive before 2000 on one menu and negative as a claim of transferable selection skill:

1. **Before 2000, on a pre-registered pre-ETF copy of the incumbent's 22-ETF menu (PRE20):**
   - On the quarterly-start long protocol, the exact rule beat VFINX after CA tax by +0.59 pp in 5-year windows (65% of 37 windows) and +0.52 pp in 10-year windows (59% of 17).
   - It beat both the equal-weight and the random-pick controls (same execution) in every yearly-start pre-2000 window.
   - Once fund distributions are taxed every year, the excess over VFINX is -1.1 to +2.6 pp depending on the window.
   - The mechanism is the incumbent's post-2010 one: it froze early into a few long-run winners. Health care alone was 23-32% of the portfolio for 40 years.
2. **Across nine sector universes in 2000-2026, on the incumbent's own protocol (`full`, CA):** the identical site rule beats on average 2.5 of 5 site-RandomPicker controls that use the identical TaxManagedCombo. On coarse sector-ETF menus (SPDR 9/11, iShares IY*, Vanguard V*) it scores -0.72 to -0.06 pp. Only on its own 22-ETF menu does it clearly beat random picks (10 of 10).
3. **Tax-managed execution, not the momentum signal, produces the CA results.** Under tax management almost any sector portfolio comes close to buy-and-hold after tax; what remains is menu composition and luck. On the Fidelity menu, random tax-managed picks match momentum overall. Momentum wins only on pre-2000 5-year windows and trails random picks after 2000.
4. **Mutual-fund menus are flattered in CA.** Fidelity Select funds distribute about 4-5%/yr, mostly capital gains, and the engine leaves this untaxed until sale. Taxing distributions yearly cuts 0.2-1.2 pp/yr from every Fidelity-menu result after 2000.

**Pre-tax (NONE):**
- Classic sector momentum on fine-grained Fidelity Select industries was strong and robust before 2000: +5 to +9 pp/yr in 5-year windows, insensitive to a 0-10 day execution lag.
- It roughly halved after 2000, is absent on coarse sector ETFs since 2000, and is fragile to parameters and to mutual-fund trading costs.
- It does not survive CA tax under standard execution.

## Data and honesty caveats specific to this family

* **Survivorship.** The Fidelity Select menu holds only funds that exist today. Merged or closed Selects (Paper & Forest, Industrial Equipment, Developing Communications, Natural Gas, Precious Metals & Minerals, ...) are missing. The equal-weight FSEL menu beat VFINX by about 2 pp/yr pre-tax over 1986-2026, which is a warning sign. Comparisons inside the menu (momentum vs random vs equal weight) are less biased than comparisons against VFINX or SPY.
* **Loads and fees.** Select funds historically carried loads and short-term trading or exchange fees, and Fidelity restricts frequent round trips. The lab charges 5+5 bp per side, so monthly-rotation results are optimistic.
* **Distributions.** The engine taxes fund distributions only at sale. Active sector funds distribute 4-5%/yr, mostly capital gains and often short-term, versus about 1.5% for SPY. This is the largest CA realism issue for this family (section 4).
* **Execution lag.** Mutual-fund signals use data through the prior close (`lag=1`) and fill at today's close. A hand check (sanity.py) confirms it: the 1999-01-04 top 3 was FDCPX/FSPTX/FSPHX, from data through 1998-12-31 with the formation window ending 1998-12-01. The site Combo, used for the incumbent's exact rule, uses today's close, as the site does.

## 8. Conclusion

* **For the user's taxable account: nothing here clears the bar.** The only CA wins come from tax-managed execution:
  - random picks and the equal-weight menu share them, so they are not evidence of sector-selection skill;
  - on mutual-fund menus they are further inflated by the engine's untaxed distributions;
  - on its own protocol, the incumbent's exact rule does no better than a random picker on 8 other sector universes.
* **For the incumbent:** the pre-2000 holdout does not contradict it on its pre-ETF analog menu.
  - There it beat its controls in every pre-2000 window and roughly matched VFINX after distribution tax.
  - But the mechanism is the same buy-early-winners-and-freeze bet, and the effect does not transfer across sector universes.
  - Treat its +0.66 pp as menu composition plus a growth/tech regime bet that happened to work on INC22, where it did beat 10 of 10 random pickers in 2000-2026, rather than as a robust momentum effect.
* **Pre-tax:** fine-grained industry momentum (Fidelity Selects) was a real pre-2000 anomaly that roughly halved afterwards. It is cost-fragile at monthly turnover, survivorship-inflated, parameter-fragile on 2000-2026, and absent on coarse sector ETFs. It is only relevant to a tax-deferred account.

## Lab issues found

1. `realism.record(cfg, regime, start, end)` accepts `end`, but `RecordingGate` keeps recording to the data end, while `_adjust_path` takes the liquidation value at `end`. The result is wrong engine and "real" CAGRs for any `end` before 2026-07-01. `verify.battery` uses the default end and is unaffected. A clipped-gate workaround in scratch reproduces cached window excess exactly.
2. `realism.adjusted()` hard-codes SPY as the benchmark, so it cannot price pre-1993 windows.
3. `realism.character()` treats all non-bond fund distributions as qualified dividends. That is lenient for active mutual funds with short-term capital-gain distributions.
4. `metrics.walk_forward(step_quarters=4)` steps over start indices, so yearly-start protocols re-select only every 4 years: 3 decisions on `screen` and 6 on `long_screen`, versus 12 on `full`.
5. Minor: the scratch label helper omits `lag=0`. Use `cfg_json` to tell lag-0 configs apart.
